findings.mechanism: The stated exercise requirement in inputs/requirements.txt mandates every saved copper track segment have width >= 0.30 mm. 0.25 mm < 0.30 mm for all five segments, so the sole evaluated criterion fails universally. Native DRC did not catch this because rc_filter.kicad_pro contains no custom rules or track-width constraints, so DRC enforced only the KiCad default minimum (0.2 mm), which 0.25 mm passes; a 0-violation DRC exit therefore does not demonstrate the requirement.
findings.reasoning: Measured directly from the native saved board file with an independent parse (python3 -I regex over the s-expression source) and corroborated by the packet geometry probe; both agree on 5 segments at 0.25 mm. The requirement is explicit, geometric, and applies to saved track segments; vias and zone fills were excluded as out of scope. Since 100% of segments violate the only stated acceptance criterion, this is a blocking defect of the exercise deliverable.
findings.title: All 5 saved copper track segments are 0.25 mm wide, violating the >= 0.30 mm exercise requirement

findings.location: work/geometry/geometry.json (criterion params empty); inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pro (empty DRC rules)
findings.mechanism: Verification gap: ERC/DRC/netlist/geometry all exited 0 with zero violations, but none of them tested width >= 0.30 mm. A reader of the check summaries alone would wrongly conclude the candidate is compliant. Encoding the limit either as a board minimum-track-width constraint or as a geometry-criterion parameter would have flagged all five segments.
findings.reasoning: This is not a tool failure (the tools ran correctly on what they were asked to check) and not an additional candidate electrical defect; it explains why the blocking width violation coexists with a clean DRC/ERC record and is recorded so the adjudicator does not treat passing checks as evidence of compliance. Labeled a concern because the review rules note a successful exit is not proof, and the gap is in check configuration rather than in the circuit itself.
findings.title: No automated check in the packet actually evaluated the 0.30 mm width criterion, so the all-green check suite masks the failure

limitations: Zone fill evaluated as saved in the read-only candidate; no refill pass was performed to confirm the fill is current (DRC on the saved state reported no issues)
No electrical simulation was run; the exercise scope is geometric and the circuit is a trivial passive RC, so function was assessed by netlist inspection only

Default KiCad DRC minimum track width (0.2 mm) is inferred from the empty rules block in rc_filter.kicad_pro and KiCad 10 defaults; the resolved internal DRC constraint value was not dumped from the tool
